text: For four years, I renewed the same health plan.
One click. Same plan. Done.
Then I compared my options. One plan: two
thousand five hundred and twenty dollars a year in
premiums. Another: just eight hundred and forty.
But here's the catch. Cheaper premiums didn't
automatically mean a better deal.
I asked the group chat. Alex said,
“Pick the best.” Danny said, “Pick the cheapest.”
If you're expecting a baby, planning surgery, seeing
specialists regularly or taking expensive medication,
the PPO could be much better. Check both
networks, your drug coverage, the exact deductible
and the out-of-pocket limits. Remember that high
expenses can arrive before your HSA has much money in it.
Back at my laptop, I didn't click “Keep my current
plan.” I checked my own numbers and made a deliberate choice.
I learned to ask: what's the bad year, what's the real
year, and where would the difference go? Forty minutes
once a year. That's a better habit than four seconds of autopilot.
If this was useful, stick around.
